title: edikt phasea verify receipt
description: Written by `bin/edikt phasea verify --plan <id>` at .edikt/state/phasea/<plan_id>.receipt.json. Records, per item, whether the sidecar-extractor's dispatch produced schema-valid, freshly-pinned output. A receipt with consumed:true is terminal: `phasea verify` MUST refuse to re-verify or re-consume the same plan_id again (exit 2). verified_at is one of two runtime-state timestamps in the phasea contract family (the other is the journal's ts); the PLAN artifact carries none — it alone is bound by ADR-020 byte-determinism.

schema_version.description: Contract version for this receipt file's on-disk shape. Integer, matching the plan schema's convention — see phasea-dispatch-plan.v1.schema.json's schema_version description.

plan_id.description: The plan this receipt verifies against. Matches exactly one phasea-dispatch-plan.v1 file's plan_id.

items.description: One entry per item in the referenced plan. A receipt always covers every planned item — there is no partial receipt that silently omits an item, because an omitted item would be indistinguishable from one that was never checked (INV-013).

item_id.description: Matches the item_id of the corresponding entry in the plan this receipt verifies.

status.description: The per-item verify outcome. "ok" — expected_output.path exists, parses as YAML, validates against gov-sidecar.v2, and its artifact_sha256 matches what was pinned in the plan (parent-hash check passed). "output-missing" — expected_output.path does not exist on disk. "schema-invalid" — the file exists and parses but fails gov-sidecar.v2 validation. "parent-hash-mismatch" — the keystone check: artifact_path's on-disk sha256 no longer equals the plan's pinned artifact_sha256, so whatever the extractor read cannot be proven to be the planned version. "prompt-version-mismatch" — the installed extractor's resolved prompt_version (ADR-055) no longer matches the plan item's pinned prompt_version, meaning the extraction contract changed between planning and verify. "failed-terminal" — this item has been re-verified attempts >= phasea.max_attempts_per_item times while still not ok, and the skill MUST NOT re-dispatch it again; the plan as a whole stays unconsumed and Phase B is refused (AC-013-3) until a human intervenes and a fresh plan is computed. "pins-unrestorable" — D6's restore step (`bin/edikt phasea restore`) could not reinstate a mandatory pinned field (e.g. `human_approved_at`) that the pre-dispatch pin-set captured on a prior sidecar, because the regenerated sidecar's shape no longer admits it or the field's prior value cannot be reconciled with the new content. Distinct from "failed-terminal": failed-terminal is a retry-exhaustion state reached after repeated re-verification, while pins-unrestorable is terminal on FIRST observation — a lost pin is never eligible for another restore attempt against the same plan_id (INV-015: governance content, including a human's prior approval, must never leave silently, and squashing this into failed-terminal would let a retry-budget count stand in for a permanent, human-visible loss).

attempts.description: How many times `phasea verify` has evaluated this item against this plan_id. Increments at verify time, not at dispatch time (owner-recommended: simpler than introducing a separate claim verb). An item already at status "ok" in a prior receipt for the same plan_id is carried forward unchanged on a later verify call — its attempts value does not increment further, because it is no longer re-evaluated.

consumed.description: True only when every item in `items` has status "ok". Setting this true is the one irreversible transition in the phasea contract: once true, this plan_id MUST be rejected by any further `phasea verify --plan <id>` invocation (exit 2), whether or not the underlying corpus later changes. A receipt with consumed:false and every remaining item at failed-terminal or pins-unrestorable represents a terminal state — also never eligible for Phase B, but distinct from CONSUMED because it never becomes eligible again for this plan_id; recovery requires a fresh plan (a corpus or config change that produces a new plan_id).

verified_at.description: ISO8601 UTC timestamp of this verify run. Runtime state, not a compiled governance surface — exempt from ADR-020's byte-determinism rule, which binds rendered/compiled output, not audit timestamps on state files.
